reason: The text features multiple regular human characters who take actions and make decisions with demonstrable agency. The Israelites respond to divine instruction and actively walk through the sea (וַיָּבֹאוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּתוֹךְ הַיָּם). Pharaoh explicitly makes decisions (וְאָמַר פַּרְעֹה) and commands pursuit of the Israelites. The Egyptian soldiers actively pursue and enter the sea. These are all human actors who take volitional actions within the narrative. However, it should be noted that while agency is present, the text's primary emphasis is on divine agency—God's control, particularly evident in the repeated hardening of Pharaoh's heart (וְחִזַּקְתִּי אֶת־לֵב־פַּרְעֹה), which constrains rather than amplifies human autonomy.
